title: From Bits to Beliefs: Recoverable Semantic Fingerprints for Black-Box Verification of Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.24084v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) can be copied, modified, and redeployed behind black-box APIs, making post-release ownership verification difficult. Existing black-box fingerprints often rely on secret query-key pairs that reproduce predefined responses, and can therefore be easily disrupted by fine-tuning, pruning, quantization, model merging, and serving-time prompt changes. We propose SimPrint, a recoverable semantic fingerprinting framework for black-box LLM ownership verification. Rather than relying on isolated exact matches, SimPrint encodes a private owner signature into a coded semantic fingerprint domain, distributing ownership evidence across natural binary question-answering probes. translated_title: 从比特到信念：用于大语言模型黑盒验证的可恢复语义指纹
translated_abstract: 开放权重的大语言模型（LLM）可能被复制、修改并通过黑盒API重新部署，这使得模型发布后的所有权验证变得困难。现有的黑盒指纹方法通常依赖于能够复现预定义响应的秘密查询-密钥对，因此很容易被微调、剪枝、量化、模型合并以及服务阶段的提示词变更所破坏。我们提出了SimPrint，一个用于黑盒LLM所有权验证的可恢复语义指纹框架。SimPrint不依赖于孤立的精确匹配，而是将私有的所有者签名编码到一个编码语义指纹域中，将所有权证据分布在自然的二元问答探针上。它通过一种低干扰的批量更新方式仅植入偏离基础模型的探针，从而保持原始模型行为，随后通过将可疑模型的响应解析为可靠比特或擦除符号，并结合纠错机制来恢复签名。
tldr: 提出SimPrint框架，将所有者签名编码为分布在自然问答探针上的可恢复语义指纹，能够抵御微调、剪枝、量化、模型合并等干扰，实现大语言模型的黑盒所有权验证。
en_tdlr: SimPrint encodes a private owner signature into recoverable semantic fingerprints distributed across natural question-answering probes, enabling robust black-box ownership verification of LLMs against fine-tuning, pruning, quantization, and model merging.
